open_obligations: Note that Wen et al. do not train critique-of-critique models via recursive reward modeling.
Check whether the discriminator-critique gap Saunders et al. define is measured at all.
Check that multiple-choice exams leave room for critiques to add information.
in.other_title: Recursive self-critiquing: critique of critique can be easier than critique, recursively
in.rationale: Saunders et al. propose training assistants that help train assistants, e.g. critiquers of critiquers. Wen et al. test whether critiquing a critique is easier than producing it and whether this holds recursively, using Human-Human, Human-AI and AI-AI experiments.
in.scope: proposed ADDRESSES: whether critiques of critiques can provide a usable supervision signal, for humans and Qwen2.5 models on multiple-choice exam tasks

text: The authors pose as future work how far critique training can be pushed relative to discriminator performance and what obstacles prevent models from explicating their knowledge. They also propose recursive reward modeling as a next step: train the base task on assisted evaluations, then treat assistance itself as a base task to train assistants that help train assistants (e.g. critiquers of critiquers).
title: Can critique training close the discriminator-critique gap? Critiquers of critiquers
